newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Austrian bonds slide on German losses, rate fears.
newsitem.headline: Austrian bonds slide on German losses, rate fears.

text.p: Austrian bonds slipped on Monday in line with the German market, prompting buying at the short end, traders said. Dealers predict a new selling wave if the German Bund future falls below 102.
Traders said the current fears of a rate hike were weighing on a lot of minds. "A small rate signal from the German Bundesbank would certainly send the market lower," said one.
* 10-year benchmark 5.625 pct bond maturing July 2007 down 50 bps at 99.70 to yield 5.66 (5.60) pct in bourse trade, quoted post-market at 99.33/43 to yield 5.71/70 pct.
* Five-year 4.625 bond maturing May 2002 down 35 bps at 99.25 to yield 4.80 (4.72) pct in bourse trade, quoted post-market at 99.10/18 to yield 4.84/82 percent.
* Austrian bond future down 40 bps at 109.30.
* 10-year spread over Germany up at seven bps, five-year lower at 20 bps.
* Money market rates three-month VIBOR just higher at 3.438 and overnight money steady at 3.13/3.38. -- Vienna newsroom, +431 53112 257
